houdini_version_notes: MPM Solver is new in Houdini 21.0; set v@v on the source before the solver.
title: Launch Velocity on MPM Source
prompt: Give MPM source material an initial throwing velocity
explanation: The MPM Solver seeds particle velocity from v@v on the incoming source geometry. Authoring it in a wrangle (rather than a constant) lets you vary the throw spatially -- e.g. by position or a paint mask -- before simulation starts.

houdini_version_notes: Post-sim visualisation; v@v is written by the MPM Solver.
title: Colour MPM Particles by Speed
prompt: Visualize MPM particle speed with a colour ramp
explanation: length(v@v) is the per-particle speed; fit() normalises it against an expected maximum, and chramp() turns that into a colour. This is the fastest way to read sim energy at a glance and to tune solver settings.

houdini_version_notes: f@Je (elastic volume ratio) is written per particle by the MPM Solver in Houdini 21; confirm the attribute name for your build.
title: Colour MPM Particles by Elastic Strain
prompt: Show compression and stretch in an MPM sim using the elastic Jacobian
explanation: The MPM solver tracks the elastic part of the deformation gradient; its determinant Je measures local volume change. abs(Je - 1) is a symmetric strain magnitude that highlights where the material is compressed or stretched -- useful for art-directing yield/fracture.

houdini_version_notes: Runs inside a solver stepping the MPM points; scale impulses by f@TimeInc to stay substep-independent.
alternative_prompts: radial force on material point particles
explosion impulse in a solver wrangle
nudge v outward from a centre
title: Custom Radial Force in an MPM Solver
prompt: Add an outward explosion impulse to MPM particles each substep
explanation: Normalising (P - center) gives an outward direction; multiplying by strength and f@TimeInc turns it into a per-substep velocity change that is independent of substep count. Clamping the distance avoids a divide-by-zero at the exact centre.

houdini_version_notes: Solver-stepped MPM points; uses f@TimeInc for substep independence.
alternative_prompts: tangential swirl in a solver wrangle
title: Vortex Force around an Axis
prompt: Swirl MPM particles around a vertical axis
explanation: The cross product of the axis and the radial vector points along the local tangent (the direction of rotation). Normalising and scaling it by strength and f@TimeInc adds a steady swirl without blowing particles outward.

houdini_version_notes: Solver-stepped MPM points; curlnoise keeps the added field divergence-free.
alternative_prompts: wispy detail for material point sim
title: Curl-Noise Turbulence on MPM Velocity
prompt: Add divergence-free turbulence to MPM particle velocity
explanation: curlnoise() returns a vector field with zero divergence, so it adds swirling detail without artificially compressing or expanding the material. Advancing the sample point by f@Time makes the turbulence evolve over the simulation.

houdini_version_notes: Solver-stepped MPM points; zeroing v anchors a region (a simple pin/glue).
title: Pin MPM Particles below a Height
prompt: Anchor MPM particles that fall below a floor height
explanation: Setting v@v to zero each substep holds those particles roughly in place, an easy way to create anchored or glued regions of a soft body without a separate constraint network. Use a smooth mask instead of a hard cutoff to avoid a visible seam.

houdini_version_notes: Set on the MPM source before the solver; drives per-particle pscale.
title: MPM Particle Radius from Density
prompt: Vary MPM particle size from an input density attribute
explanation: fit() remaps the incoming density into a sensible radius band so denser regions sample with larger or smaller particles as desired. Controlling pscale at the source is the cleanest way to balance detail against solve cost.
